profile.a: The author, writing a reflective diary for the Negotiations Lab.
Which negotiation strategies worked across five simulations and what the author learned about himself and others.
Lent term 2025; handed in on 17 March 2025.

Simulations covering a real-estate deal, a US-Asian joint venture, a contract dispute, an African airport partnership and the World Trade Center rebuild; plenaries with an ISS astronaut and on Brexit.
Negotiation is treated as a life skill that combines communication, judgement, decision-making and conflict resolution.
Each case is read through the five core books (Fisher, Ury and Patton; Kahneman; Malhotra; Stone, Patton and Heen; Voss) plus wider reading on emotion, coalitions and power.

charts.title: What the author learned about himself

items.title: Preparation
items.text: Reading cases and related news in depth paid off; peers who relied on AI summaries underperformed.

items.title: Do not assume
items.text: The PowerScreen video made Hacker look reactive; focusing on the other side's psychology removed the bias.

items.title: Quantify
items.text: Weighted spreadsheets and the 9-dimension worksheet kept slow, deliberate thinking in charge.

items.title: Sequence and frame
items.text: Early on he stated positions too directly; the order and context of options matter.

items.title: Use information and power
items.text: Listening revealed the bank's veto, which was then used boldly.

items.title: Separate must-haves
items.text: Distinguishing preferable from unacceptable outcomes rescued the WTC negotiation.

items.title: Astronaut training
items.text: Timely, factual communication and teamwork keep elite teams safe in high-stakes settings.

items.title: Brexit negotiations
items.text: Read as a failure of risk assessment, over-reliance on polls and missing contingency plans, especially for Northern Ireland.
